discovery: Prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and their quantized dissipationless edge transport (quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects)

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases and quantum transport
motivation: Kane (with Mele) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator with a Z2 invariant and helical edge states. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental proof in HgTe/CdTe quantum wells, measuring quantized edge conductance of about 2e^2/h. Xue's group then realized the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulator films, where the Hall resistance is quantized at h/e^2 with no external magnetic field. Together these results opened a new field: topological band theory now classifies materials, and quantized transport survives disorder and real-device imperfections. It became a worldwide experimental and theoretical effort on Majorana platforms, axion electrodynamics and low-dissipation electronics. Few discoveries since the quantum Hall effect have reshaped condensed matter physics so deeply, or tied abstract topology so directly to precise, reproducible measurements.
